analysis_notes.gap_analysis_detail: Torah 111 (LM2) is an extremely brief reported saying — two short episodes with no structured conceptual discourse. The text contains no explicit bechina language (no בְּחִינַת, no הוּא בְּחִינַת, no נִקְרָא used as bechina markers). Episode one records a questioner who could not study Torah; the Rebbe replied that through תְּפִלָּה (prayer) one can arrive at everything — לְתוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה וּלְכָל הַקְּדֻשּׁוֹת וּלְכָל הָעֲבוֹדוֹת וּלְכָל הַטּוֹבוֹת שֶׁבְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת. This is an eitza (cause-and-effect) statement — prayer produces or enables access to Torah and avodah — not a bechina equivalence between prayer and those concepts. Prayer does not share the essential nature of Torah; rather, prayer leads to Torah. Episode two states that if a dead person were allowed to return to this world to pray, he would certainly pray beautifully with all his strength. This is a rhetorical emphasis on the value of prayer, with no conceptual equivalence declared between any two nodes. No missing bechina nodes are identified. The dataset correctly records zero bechina edges for reference 1111.
